square.name: Village square
square.desc: A packed-earth square around a stone well. A notice post leans by the well; a few hens scratch in the dust. The forge rings to the east, the inn's sign creaks to the south, and the church stands north.
items: notice (a faded sheet nailed to the post)
square.gm_notes: The notice announces the Harvest Feast in a fortnight and asks for a volunteer to carry the church's bell-rope to the mill for mending. Anyone lowering themselves into the well must find a way: the bucket rope is frayed.

well_bottom.name: Bottom of the well
well_bottom.desc: Cold water to the knees, slick stones, a smell of iron. A gap in the wall breathes air from somewhere dark.
well_bottom.gm_notes: Getting down without rope or help should cost a scrape or a wetting. The rusted key opens the manor cellar's inner door.

old_cellar.name: Forgotten cellar
old_cellar.desc: A vaulted cellar under something large. Barrels long empty, a stair blocked by a fallen beam, and an iron-bound door.
old_cellar.gm_notes: The iron door is locked; the rusted key from the well opens it. Without the key it does not budge.

manor_vault.name: Manor vault
manor_vault.desc: A dry stone room under the manor. A strongbox, a rack of mildewed ledgers, and a narrow stair upward.
manor_vault.gm_notes: The ledger records that the old lord left the mill to Wat's mother, not to the reeve — the reeve suppressed it. Reading it sets the flag ledger_read. Taking coin from the strongbox is theft: honesty -2.

church_yard.name: Churchyard
church_yard.desc: Leaning headstones in long grass, a yew older than the church. The church door stands open; a path runs on north to the fields.
church_yard.gm_notes: One fresh grave, unmarked, near the wall: Merrow's son, buried this spring.

yew_hollow.name: Hollow of the yew
yew_hollow.desc: The great yew is hollow inside, big enough to crouch in. Someone has left a child's wooden horse and a handful of pebbles here.
yew_hollow.gm_notes: Wat's hiding place. Opens when the player asks Wat about where he goes, or looks closely behind the yew with curiosity high.

church.name: Church of St. Wystan
church.desc: Whitewashed walls, a painted rood, a bell-rope hanging slack from the tower. Candles gutter by a side altar.
church.gm_notes: The bell-rope is the one the notice mentions. Aldric is usually here.

bell_tower.name: Bell tower
bell_tower.desc: A ladder of worn rungs up to the bell. From the louvres you can see the whole village, the fen to the east, and the road running away west.
bell_tower.gm_notes: From here the player can see smoke in the fen and, at dusk, something large moving in it (the wyrm). Looking sets flag seen_fen.

forge.name: The forge
forge.desc: Heat, soot, the smell of quenched iron. An anvil, a trough, tools hung in careful order. A cot in the corner is neatly made.
forge.gm_notes: Merrow's forge. Taking tools without asking is theft: honesty -1.

forge_yard.name: Forge yard
forge_yard.desc: A scrap heap, a chained dog asleep in the shade, and a cart missing a wheel.
forge_yard.gm_notes: The dog is old and friendly if approached kindly; compassion +1 for feeding or freeing it, but freeing it upsets Merrow unless asked.

inn_common.name: The Drowned Ox, common room
inn_common.desc: Low beams, a smoking hearth, benches sticky with old ale. A stair leads up; a door leads to the kitchen.
inn_common.gm_notes: Tobin's inn. Ale costs a penny; the player has none unless they earn or find some.

inn_kitchen.name: Inn kitchen
inn_kitchen.desc: A great pot, hanging onions, a back door propped open onto the lane. A cat watches from the flour sacks.
inn_kitchen.gm_notes: Taking food is theft unless offered: honesty -1. Tobin offers bread freely to anyone who does him a kindness.

inn_upstairs.name: Inn, upstairs
inn_upstairs.desc: A short passage with three doors. One stands ajar on a bare room; one is locked; the third is Tobin's own.
inn_upstairs.gm_notes: The locked room holds the pedlar's abandoned trunk. Tobin has the key.

inn_room.name: Bare room
inn_room.desc: A straw mattress, a window over the square, a crack in the shutter you could watch the whole village through.

inn_locked.name: The pedlar's room
inn_locked.desc: Dust, a trunk, a smell of camphor. The pedlar never came back for it.
inn_locked.gm_notes: The trunk holds a bolt of red cloth, a set of tin whistles, and a letter in a hand nobody here can read except Aldric. Tobin unlocks the room for someone he trusts.

lane.name: Back lane
lane.desc: A muddy lane between garden walls. Herbs spill over one wall; a gate stands open to a cottage garden. The lane runs on to the mill.

herb_garden.name: Ysolde's garden
herb_garden.desc: Beds of sage, rue, feverfew, and things with no names you know. A low cottage with its door open, drying bundles hung under the eaves.
herb_garden.gm_notes: Ysolde's home. She is often here or inside.

herb_cottage.name: Ysolde's cottage
herb_cottage.desc: One room, dim and fragrant. Jars on every shelf, a cat-skull on the sill, a bed under a loft ladder.

herb_loft.name: Ysolde's loft
herb_loft.desc: Bundled herbs, a small chest, a round window onto the fields.
items: small chest (a book of receipts, some in a strange script)
herb_loft.gm_notes: The book contains Ysolde's real learning: she was trained in the city, not by a hedge-witch. Opens when Ysolde trusts the player.

mill_yard.name: Mill yard
mill_yard.desc: The great wheel turns slow in the millrace. Sacks stacked under a lean-to, a ladder to the loft, and the mill door.
mill_yard.gm_notes: The mill belongs, in law, to the reeve, who is away. Wat works it. The reeve's man collects the toll on feast days.

mill.name: Inside the mill
mill.desc: Flour in the air, the groan of the stones, a shaft turning overhead. Everything shakes a little.

mill_loft.name: Mill loft
mill_loft.desc: Sacks and pigeons. A hole in the boards looks straight down on the stones.

river_bank.name: River bank
river_bank.desc: Willows, a mooring post with no boat, and the river sliding brown toward the fen. A path goes on into reeds.

fields.name: The fields
fields.desc: Strips of barley and beans running to a hedge. A sheepfold, a scarecrow in a good coat, and a track east toward the fen and west toward the road.
fields.gm_notes: Taking the coat is petty theft (honesty -1) but the scarecrow does not mind.

sheepfold.name: Sheepfold
sheepfold.desc: A dry-stone ring, a dozen sheep, a shepherd's hut with nobody in it.
sheepfold.gm_notes: Two sheep have been taken this month; the villagers blame wolves. It was the wyrm.

fen_edge.name: Edge of the fen
fen_edge.desc: Reeds taller than a man, standing water, a raised path of old logs going in. Something large has flattened the reeds to the north.
fen_edge.gm_notes: The fen is the wyrm's country. Entering sets flag entered_fen.

fen_island.name: Island in the fen
fen_island.desc: A hummock of dry ground with an alder on it, ringed by black water. Bones of sheep. A cave-mouth under the roots, breathing warm air.
fen_island.gm_notes: The wyrm's lair is under the roots. It is old, slow, and lonely, not a monster of legend; it can be fought, bargained with, or befriended. Any approach sets flag wyrm_met.

wyrm_cave.name: The wyrm's cave
wyrm_cave.desc: Warm, dark, and rank. Something enormous breathes in the dark, and two eyes open like lamps.
wyrm_cave.gm_notes: The wyrm speaks, slowly, in an old dialect. It wants to be left alone and to be remembered. Killing it (only possible with real cunning or a weapon and great cost) sets flag wyrm_dead; making peace sets wyrm_peace. If the player has no reserve NPC assigned as the wyrm, narrate it yourself.

road.name: The west road
road.desc: A rutted road between hedges, a milestone worn blank, and the village falling behind. It goes on a long way.

road_far.name: Far along the road
road_far.desc: The village is a smudge behind you. Ahead, a crossroads and a gibbet with nothing on it. You could keep going.
road_far.gm_notes: If the player chooses to keep going and leave for good, set flag left_village. Ask once, plainly, whether they mean to leave; if yes, it is an ending.

manor_hall.name: Manor hall
manor_hall.desc: A shuttered hall with dust-sheets over everything. The lord is dead and the reeve keeps the keys. A stair goes down; the great door is barred from outside.
manor_hall.gm_notes: Reachable only from below. The barred door can be unbarred from inside, which opens the manor to the square (add an exit if the player does it).
